background.summary: Current finance workflows are spread across Excel, email, ERP, and manual approvals, creating inconsistent data, low approval efficiency, and lagging budget control. A unified finance management capability is needed.
background.objective: Create a unified finance business entry point, improve approval and payment efficiency, provide end-to-end budget control, and meet audit trail requirements.

core_scenarios: Employees initiate expense or payment requests and track progress.
Department owners approve business requests and confirm budget reasonableness.
Finance reviews documents, invoices, and contract attachments.
Approved requests enter the payment process and payment results are recorded.
Business data flows into ledgers and reports for analysis and audit.

functional_requirements.overview: The requirement focuses on six capabilities: application, approval, budget control, invoice/document management, payment management, and reporting analytics, with the goal of connecting the finance processing chain.

feature_details.description: Supports the initiation, draft saving, submission, withdrawal, and copying of expense, reimbursement, and payment requests.
feature_details.trigger: The user clicks New Request and submits the form.
feature_details.processing_logic: The system validates required fields, amount format, and attachment completeness, generates a request number, and routes the request to the next process.

feature_details.description: Supports multi-level approval, countersignature, additional signature, rejection, and timeout reminders.
feature_details.trigger: A submitted request automatically enters the approval flow.
feature_details.processing_logic: The system routes the request according to organization structure and approval rules, and approval results drive status changes.

feature_details.description: Performs budget validation, reservation, release, and warning during request and finance review stages.
feature_details.trigger: Triggered when a request is submitted or reviewed by finance.
feature_details.processing_logic: The system checks budget balances by department, project, and expense category. Over-budget items enter special approval or warning flows.

feature_details.description: Supports invoice information entry, attachment upload, duplicate checking, and document association.
feature_details.trigger: Triggered when users upload documents or finance reviews documents.
feature_details.processing_logic: The system validates document completeness and consistency, maintains document status, and links documents to request forms.
exception_cases: Invoice amount inconsistent with request amount

feature_details.description: Supports payment review, payment execution, status write-back, and voucher archiving.
feature_details.trigger: Starts after finance review is approved.
feature_details.processing_logic: The system validates payee information and payment conditions, records payment status, and archives payment vouchers.

feature_details.description: Provides report query and export capabilities across expense, budget, and payment dimensions.
feature_details.trigger: Triggered when users query reports or the system performs scheduled summaries.
feature_details.processing_logic: The system supports multidimensional filtering, summary display, and export for financial analysis and management decisions.

business_rules: Every request must be associated with expense category, department, occurrence date, and other basic information.
Over-budget requests cannot pass directly and must enter special approval or strong reminder flows.
Invoices, contracts, and payment vouchers must be associated with request forms and archived.
Finance review starts only after approval is passed, and payment starts only after finance review is passed.
The same business request cannot be submitted for payment repeatedly.
After payment is completed, request status must automatically update to Paid or an equivalent status.

interaction_flow: The user creates and submits a request.
The system validates required fields, budget, and attachment completeness.
Approvers complete approval, then finance performs review.
After review passes, the request enters payment processing and the final result is written back.
Data is synchronized into reports and ledgers.

risks_and_notes: Inconsistent historical finance data may affect migration and reconciliation.
Complex approval rules may affect rollout if not clarified early.
Unstable external system interfaces may affect budget or payment result synchronization.
acceptance_criteria: The request, approval, review, payment, and archive process can run end to end.
Budget validation logic meets business expectations.
Invoice duplicate checking and attachment validation rules take effect.
Report data is consistent with business document data.
Permission isolation is correct and unauthorized access is blocked.
All key nodes have audit logs.
open_questions: Is real-time bidirectional synchronization with ERP required?
Should over-budget scenarios be blocked or routed through special approval?
Does invoice validation need to connect to an external verification capability?
Should report statistics follow finance definitions or business definitions?
